Bridge and Structural Trades

Ironworkers (IW), IUPAT bridge painters, IUOE operating engineers and LIUNA on the deck

OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts M (fall protection), R (steel erection) and CC (cranes); 1926.62 lead in construction for bridge coatings; ANSI Z359; AWS D1.5 bridge welding; the owner's lane-closure and MUTCD traffic control plan

The bridge as a workplace: cable and hanger inspection at height, lead-paint containment on a truss, deck joint replacement under traffic control, and the erection work the structural programme already teaches.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1620lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Bridge Cable Inspection

13 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.2 min

The inspection that finds what connecting never checks: two lanyards live on the traveller, the rope read by eye and by flux head, and the wire count carried against the rejection criterion.

  • AASHTO — AASHTO Manual for Bridge Element Inspection and the LRFD Bridge Design Specifications
  • union — Ironworkers and IMPACT — apprenticeship and safety training for structural, ornamental and reinforcing ironwork
  • NBIS — 23 CFR Part 650 Subpart C — National Bridge Inspection Standards
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926 — Safety and health regulations for construction

Construction & Structural Trades

Bridge Lead Containment

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.5 min

The coatings work the same bridge eventually needs: a truss bay contained and held negative over open water so the lead that comes off it never reaches the water below.

  • union — IUPAT Finishing Trades Institute — industrial painter, glazier and drywall finisher apprenticeship, including lead and containment training
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.62 — Lead in construction
  • RCRA — 40 CFR Part 261 — Identification and listing of hazardous waste
  • RCRA — 40 CFR Part 262 — Standards applicable to generators of hazardous waste, including the manifest
  • SSPC — SSPC-QP 2 — Qualification procedure for painting contractors removing hazardous coatings in the field from complex structures, now administered by AMPP
  • SSPC — SSPC-SP 10 / NACE No. 2 — Near-white metal blast cleaning
  • SSPC — SSPC-SP surface preparation standards (SP 1 to SP 11), now published by AMPP

Deck Joint Replacement

13 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.1153 — Respirable crystalline silica in construction

Structural Bolting & Torque

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

The bolt-up the connecting leaves behind: a girder field splice verified in the calibrator, snugged from the middle out, turned from its match marks, and the one bolt that spun found before the inspector reads the rest.

Bearing Replacement & Jacking

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.2 min

The maintenance the bearings eventually need: the lane under the span closed, a girder jacked on the engineer's plan with cribbing tight beside the jack, and the girder let down onto its new bearing without ever hanging on oil alone.

What it proves

Competency: Inspect, contain and rebuild structural steel and bridge deck work

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 7 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M Fall protection; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart R Steel erection; OSHA 29 CFR 1926.62 Lead in construction; AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code; ANSI/ASSP Z359 Fall Protection Code.

These stations also count toward:

  • Fall Protection (2 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Respiratory Protection — selection, proving and working on air (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts M (fall protection), R (steel erection) and CC (cranes); 1926.62 lead in construction for bridge coatings; ANSI Z359; AWS D1.5 bridge welding; the owner's lane-closure and MUTCD traffic control plan. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
